---

##### `location`<sup>Optional</sup> <a name="location" id="@cdktn/provider-google.dataGoogleContainerCluster.DataGoogleContainerCluster.Initializer.parameter.location"></a>

- *Type:* java.lang.String

The location (region or zone) in which the cluster master will be created, as well as the default node location.

If you specify a zone (such as us-central1-a), the cluster will be a zonal cluster with a single cluster master. If you specify a region (such as us-west1), the cluster will be a regional cluster with multiple masters spread across zones in the region, and with default node locations in those zones as well.

Docs at Terraform Registry: {@link https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/google/7.42.0/docs/data-sources/container_cluster#location DataGoogleContainerCluster#location}

---

##### `project`<sup>Optional</sup> <a name="project" id="@cdktn/provider-google.dataGoogleContainerCluster.DataGoogleContainerCluster.Initializer.parameter.project"></a>

- *Type:* java.lang.String

The ID of the project in which the resource belongs.

If it is not provided, the provider project is used.

Docs at Terraform Registry: {@link https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/google/7.42.0/docs/data-sources/container_cluster#project DataGoogleContainerCluster#project}

##### `isConstruct` <a name="isConstruct" id="@cdktn/provider-google.dataGoogleContainerCluster.DataGoogleContainerCluster.isConstruct"></a>

```java
import io.cdktn.providers.google.data_google_container_cluster.DataGoogleContainerCluster;

DataGoogleContainerCluster.isConstruct(java.lang.Object x)
```

Checks if `x` is a construct.

Use this method instead of `instanceof` to properly detect `Construct`
instances, even when the construct library is symlinked.

Explanation: in JavaScript, multiple copies of the `constructs` library on
disk are seen as independent, completely different libraries. As a
consequence, the class `Construct` in each copy of the `constructs` library
is seen as a different class, and an instance of one class will not test as
`instanceof` the other class. `npm install` will not create installations
like this, but users may manually symlink construct libraries together or
use a monorepo tool: in those cases, multiple copies of the `constructs`
library can be accidentally installed, and `instanceof` will behave
unpredictably. It is safest to avoid using `instanceof`, and using
this type-testing method instead.

###### `x`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="x" id="@cdktn/provider-google.dataGoogleContainerCluster.DataGoogleContainerCluster.isConstruct.parameter.x"></a>

- *Type:* java.lang.Object

Any object.

##### `location`<sup>Optional</sup> <a name="location" id="@cdktn/provider-google.dataGoogleContainerCluster.DataGoogleContainerClusterConfig.property.location"></a>

```java
public java.lang.String getLocation();
```

- *Type:* java.lang.String

The location (region or zone) in which the cluster master will be created, as well as the default node location.

If you specify a zone (such as us-central1-a), the cluster will be a zonal cluster with a single cluster master. If you specify a region (such as us-west1), the cluster will be a regional cluster with multiple masters spread across zones in the region, and with default node locations in those zones as well.

Docs at Terraform Registry: {@link https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/google/7.42.0/docs/data-sources/container_cluster#location DataGoogleContainerCluster#location}

---
